title: UraLex 2.0 — Indo-Iranian contact-layer calibration for Uralic (BEAST2)

calibrated_node.definition: Most recent common ancestor (MRCA) of all sampled Uralic varieties EXCEPT the Samoyedic branch; i.e. the node uniting Finnic + Saami + Mordvin + Mari + Permic + Ugric.
calibrated_node.monophyly_assumption: Requires Finno-Ugric to be monophyletic (Samoyedic as the outgroup / first split). Enforce as a monophyly constraint or define the calibration on this MRCA taxon set.
calibrated_node.support: The core Indo-Iranian layer reaches ALL SIX Finno-Ugric branches. Ugric's participation rests chiefly on 'horn' 40-a (probable) and 'house' 26-b (possible); no Ugric core-II loan is coded 'clear'. See the conservative alternative node for the clear-only reading.

alternative_conservative_node.when_to_prefer: Prefer this if you anchor ONLY on UraLex 'clear' loans and treat Ugric's participation in the oldest Indo-Iranian layer as unproven.
alternative_conservative_node.definition: MRCA of Finnic + Saami + Mordvin + Mari + Permic (Ugric and Samoyedic excluded).
alternative_conservative_node.support: The set of UraLex 'clear' core Indo-Iranian loans collectively spans exactly these five branches (e.g. 'good' 57-b: Saami/Mordvin/Mari/Permic; 'green' 138-a: Finnic/Mari/Permic), and none reaches Ugric or Samoyed.
alternative_conservative_node.effect: Shifts the calibrated node one level shallower (drops Ugric). The ~4000 BP minimum-age bound and its direction are UNCHANGED; only which taxa bound the node moves.

calibration.anchor_event: Proto-Indo-Iranian ('Aryan') loanword contact layer entering Finno-Ugric
calibration.anchor_age_basis: Proto-Indo-Iranian is dated to c. 2000 BCE on independent archaeological (Sintashta c. 2100-1800 BCE, early Andronovo horizon) and historical-linguistic grounds; c. 2000 BCE ~= 4000 years before present.
calibration.constraint_direction_reasoning: The loans entered branches that had ALREADY begun their own sound changes (they surface with regular BRANCH-SPECIFIC reflexes, not one uniform proto-form), so the Finno-Ugric crown had already split into its daughter branches by the time of contact. Therefore the crown's divergence PRE-DATES the contact: age(FU crown) >= age(contact) ~= 4000 BP. This is a lower bound, not a point age.
calibration.not_proto_uralic_because: The clear/core Indo-Iranian loans are confined to Finno-Ugric and are essentially absent from Samoyedic. The handful of Samoyed-touching records do not pattern as clean vertical inheritance (see caveats), so the contact does not reach below the Samoyed split, i.e. not the Uralic root.
calibration.deeper_than_branch_protolanguages_becaus: The same loan layer is shared ACROSS the Finno-Ugric branches (Finnic, Saami, Mordvin, Mari, Permic, Ugric), so it constrains their common ancestor, which is deeper than any single branch proto-language (Proto-Finnic, Proto-Saami, ...).

beast2_prior.target: tmrca of the Finno-Ugric crown node (see mrca_taxon_set)
beast2_prior.interpretation: node age (time before present) >= 4000 years; true age older, tail open

recommended_prior.note: Hard minimum at 4000 BP with a decaying tail into older ages; encodes 'at least 4000, probably somewhat older, no hard maximum'. Mean above offset is a soft modelling choice, not derived from the loan evidence.

alternatives.note: Non-committal minimum; upper bound is an arbitrary loose cap, adjust to taste.
Use if you want most mass just above the bound with a long right tail.

beast2_prior.caution: Do NOT encode this as a point age or a two-sided normal centred on 4000: the evidence gives a floor, not an estimate, of the node's age.
beast2_prior.ascertainment_note: The matrix contains only observed/variable cognate characters (constant-in-all-taxa characters were dropped); use BEAST2's binary model with ascertainment-bias correction accordingly.
beast2_prior.proto_uralic_tip_note: Proto-Uralic* is a partial reconstruction, not a contemporaneous tip. Prefer treating it as an ancestral/root constraint or drop it from tip-dating rather than dating it as a leaf.

branch_specific_reflex_evidence.point: The one loan surfaces as Finnic sarvi, Saami coarvi, Mari sur, Mordvin suro, Permic sur, Ugric (Hung.) szarv: the regular, DIFFERING per-branch outcomes of Proto-Uralic *s and the branch vowel systems. The loan therefore post-dates or coincides with branch formation rather than being a single unaltered proto-form, supporting a node that had already begun to diversify by contact time.

caveats_and_sensitivity.detail: An Indo-Iranian-flagged set reaches Finnic and Samoyed but SKIPS every intermediate Finno-Ugric branch (Saami, Mordvin, Mari, Permic, Ugric). A single borrowing into undivided Proto-Uralic would predict intermediate reflexes; their absence makes parallel/areal borrowing or a Wanderwort more likely. Marked 'probable', and the Nganasan form is not even loan-flagged. Hence it does not license a Proto-Uralic-level (Samoyed-inclusive) calibration.
caveats_and_sensitivity.effect_on_call: Does not move the node below the Samoyed split.

caveats_and_sensitivity.detail: A single-language, later-'Iranian' (post-split) loan into Selkup; younger layer, irrelevant to the deep node.

caveats_and_sensitivity.issue: UraLex Proto-Uralic* reconstructions attached to II-loan sets (e.g. 40-a *sarwi)
caveats_and_sensitivity.detail: The compilers attach a Proto-Uralic* reconstruction to some II-loan etyma. This reflects their maximal etymological depth judgement, not proof of Samoyed-inclusive inheritance; the attested reflex distribution (absent from Samoyed) is the primary signal used here.
caveats_and_sensitivity.effect_on_call: Node kept at FU crown, not Uralic root.

caveats_and_sensitivity.detail: Hungarian in particular has famous LATER Iranian/Alanic loans. Those are excluded from the core-II anchor; Ugric still participates in the core Indo-Iranian layer (e.g. shares 'horn' 40-a and 'house' 26-b), so the crown remains inclusive of Ugric.
caveats_and_sensitivity.effect_on_call: Ugric retained inside the calibrated clade.

caveats_and_sensitivity.detail: If one instead judged the loans to have entered a still-UNDIVIDED proto-language, the same 4000 BP date would become a MAXIMUM (upper) bound on that node. We follow the phonological evidence (regular branch-specific reflexes) that the branches were already differentiating, which makes 4000 BP a MINIMUM on the FU crown.
caveats_and_sensitivity.effect_on_call: Determines lower- vs upper-bound; we use lower bound.

one_line_summary: The Indo-Iranian (Proto-Indo-Iranian, ~4000 BP) loan layer is shared across all six Finno-Ugric branches but essentially absent from Samoyedic and shows branch-specific reflexes; it therefore places a MINIMUM age of ~4000 BP on the Finno-Ugric crown node (deeper than any branch proto-language, shallower than Proto-Uralic).
